research_question: Among term or preterm neonates up to 28 days of age undergoing a painful procedure (e.g., heel lance, venipuncture, intramuscular or intradermal injection), what is the effect of direct breastfeeding or breast milk administered during the procedure, compared with no intervention/routine care without an analgesic or comfort measure, on total crying duration during and immediately after the procedure?
treatment_label: Direct breastfeeding or breast milk given during the painful procedure
control_label: No intervention (routine care, no analgesic, and no comfort measure)
outcome_description: Total duration of crying in seconds during and immediately after the painful procedure, including crying time or duration of first cry as defined by the paper. Extract the mean, SD, and number of neonates in each eligible arm. If several crying measures are reported, prefer total crying time over latency to first cry; exclude pain scores, percentage of time crying, and all physiological or other outcomes. Convert minutes to seconds and record both the original unit and conversion. Convert SE/SEM to SD using SD = SE × sqrt(n), after checking table footnotes to determine whether “±” denotes SD or SE. If only a median with range or interquartile range is available, estimate the mean and SD using a recognized standard method and document the method and assumptions. Use one row per trial; if results are given separately for multiple procedures, use the primary procedure.
positive_direction: For standardized effect orientation, a positive Hedges g would mean shorter crying duration and therefore favor breastfeeding; for the user-requested raw mean difference calculated as breastfeeding minus control, MD < 0 seconds means less crying and favors breastfeeding.
search_queries: breastfeeding breast milk neonatal procedural pain crying duration randomized trial
breastfeeding neonate heel lance venipuncture crying time controlled trial
expressed breast milk newborn painful procedure crying duration quasi-randomized
inclusion_criteria: Original randomized or quasi-randomized controlled trials enrolling term or preterm neonates up to 28 days of age who undergo a painful procedure such as heel lance, venipuncture, or intramuscular/intradermal injection.
Trials comparing direct breastfeeding or breast milk administered during the procedure with an eligible no-intervention condition (routine care, no analgesia, and no comfort measure).

Trials reporting total crying duration during and/or immediately after the procedure, or sufficient quantitative information from which a mean difference in seconds and its variance can be obtained or estimated.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study, including systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, protocols without results, and theoretical papers.

No comparison between the eligible breastfeeding/breast-milk treatment and a no-intervention control; this includes studies with only active controls such as sucrose, glucose, water, positioning, non-nutritive sucking, or skin-to-skin contact without breastfeeding, as well as studies in older infants or without randomized/quasi-randomized allocation.

No quantitative crying-duration outcome data capable of producing an effect size (e.g., means and SDs or convertible SEs, t/F statistics, usable medians with ranges/IQRs, proportions, or odds ratios); studies reporting only pain scores, percentage of time crying, physiological outcomes, or latency to first cry when no eligible total crying duration is available are excluded.
Completely unrelated to breastfeeding or breast milk for procedural pain in neonates.
moderators_to_extract: intervention mode (direct breastfeeding versus expressed breast milk)
timing and duration of breastfeeding/breast-milk administration relative to the procedure
effect_size_note: Pool raw mean differences in seconds using a random-effects model, defined as mean crying duration in the breastfeeding group minus mean crying duration in the no-intervention group; therefore MD < 0 favors breastfeeding. Extract only the breastfeeding and true no-intervention arms from multi-arm trials, regardless of column order, and use the same breastfeeding group only once against the no-intervention group. Convert all time units to seconds before analysis. Apply documented SD conversions or standard mean/SD estimators where necessary. Use one independent comparison per trial and the primary procedure when multiple procedures are reported. Assess heterogeneity (tau-squared and I-squared), present 95% confidence intervals and a forest plot, conduct sensitivity analyses for quasi-randomized trials and imputed summary statistics where feasible, assess risk of bias using an appropriate randomized-trial tool, and examine reporting bias only if enough studies are available.
